title: Scalable Sub-Quadratic Architectures for Million-Token Language Modeling: Attention, Extrapolation, and Persistent Memory
background:
Transformer-based language models have become the dominant paradigm in NLP, yet their quadratic self-attention complexity in sequence length remains a fundamental bottleneck for processing book-length documents, multi-document corpora, long-horizon agent traces, and code repositories. Recent advances have explored three complementary directions. First, sub-quadratic attention surrogates such as state-space models and linear recurrences (e.g., Mamba-style selective SSMs [1]) and gated linear attention variants [2] achieve near-linear scaling but exhibit measurable degradation on retrieval-heavy tasks like needle-in-a-haystack and multi-hop reasoning. Second, position-encoding interventions such as YaRN-style RoPE rescaling and attention-sink calibration [3] enable partial length extrapolation but typically require continued pretraining and still collapse beyond 4-8x the training context. Third, memory-augmented architectures combining KV compression, hierarchical caches, and retrieval-based external memory [4][5] reduce activation footprint yet introduce recall-staleness trade-offs and brittle routing under distribution shift.

Despite this progress, no existing approach simultaneously delivers (i) faithful million-token recall, (ii) training-free extrapolation from short-context pretraining, and (iii) wall-clock and memory efficiency competitive with modern dense Transformers. Recent benchmarks such as RULER and LongProc [6] reveal that reported perplexity gains often fail to translate into downstream long-context reasoning, and that current evaluations conflate retrieval, aggregation, and generation. The community lacks principled theory connecting state capacity, expressivity, and recall fidelity, as well as systems-level co-design of kernels, memory hierarchies, and decoding strategies tailored to ultra-long contexts. Closing these gaps is essential for scientific document understanding, legal and biomedical reasoning, and persistent-memory agents.
challenges: Designing sub-quadratic attention or state-space mixers that provably preserve associative recall and multi-hop retrieval at sequence lengths exceeding 1M tokens, without falling back to dense attention over critical spans

Achieving training-free or minimal-finetuning length extrapolation by 30x or more beyond the pretraining window, addressing attention-sink drift, RoPE high-frequency aliasing, and softmax entropy collapse in a unified framework
Co-designing hierarchical KV-cache compression, eviction, and retrieval policies that bound GPU memory to O(sqrt(N)) or better while maintaining bounded approximation error on long-range dependencies
Developing hardware-aware IO-efficient kernels (FlashAttention-style) for hybrid SSM-attention stacks that sustain >50% MFU on million-token sequences across heterogeneous accelerators

Building diagnostic benchmarks that disentangle retrieval, aggregation, ordering, and abstractive reasoning over long contexts, replacing perplexity and synthetic needle tests as the primary evaluation signal
